transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Daniel Park (NovoMetric CTO); Sofia Martinez (ML Lead); Rajesh Kumar (Platform Eng); Maria Lopez (Procurement)

Summary:
- Goal: scope a 2-week benchmark sprint to validate TTFT (time-to-first-token) and TPOT (time-per-token) SLOs for NovoMetric chat assistant workload; prioritize which SLOs matter to business vs engineering and agree on measurement plan and timeline.
- Key tradeoffs discussed: strict p95 TTFT for interactive UX vs p99 TPOT for batch/summary endpoints; caching and batching impact; need for representative traffic sampling.
- Agreed next steps and owners for traffic export, template, infra prep, and scheduling.

Topics covered:
1) Business success criteria and stakeholder alignment
2) Workload sizing and traffic decomposition (prompt/response lengths, burstiness)
3) SLO definitions: TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99, weighted latencies for different routes
4) Measurement plan: synthetic vs replayed, sampling windows, warm cache vs cold cache runs
5) Timeline and sprint logistics.

Action items (captured for the call): see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45, 50 minutes, try to get a sprint plan nailed down. quick intros?
[00:00:08] Daniel: yeah hi, daniel here, cto at novometric, i'll be the exec sponsor, we'll have sofia run the ml side and rajesh do infra, maria is here for procurement stuff.
[00:00:20] Sofia: hi all, sofia — we're looking to make the assistant feel snappy for our analysts, so first token matters. But also we have async summarization flows where total token cost is the priority.
[00:00:32] Priya: cool, that maps nicely to the TTFT vs TPOT tradeoff. alex and i are going to propose an SLO matrix and a measurement plan.
[00:00:41] Maria: quick note from procurement — we'll need an SOW and a rough estimate for the pilot cost.
[00:00:47] Alex: yep, we'll include a pilot budget estimate once we pick the runner infra and expected throughput.

[00:02:05] Alex: first question — what are your primary routes right now? live chat, agent followups, batch summarization? maybe percent split?
[00:02:15] Sofia: we have three top routes: interactive chat (around 60% of calls), long-form summarization (20%), and data-enrichment (20%) which is more batch but time-sensitive. note those numbers wobble a bit during EOD.
[00:02:34] Rajesh: and burstiness is pretty strong — we see sudden spikes when market reports drop, plus daily morning ramp.
[00:02:42] Alex: good, that's the traffic profile we need. can you give us rough prompt/response length histograms?
[00:02:48] Sofia: yes, typical prompts are 30–80 tokens, responses vary: interactive is usually 40–200 tokens, summarization can be 500–1,200 tokens. we'll produce a CSV.

[00:04:10] Priya: ok, so for TTFT do you care about p50 vs p95 vs p99? many teams pick p95 for interactive UX and p99 as a guardrail. what do you think?
[00:04:22] Daniel: our product VP wants 200ms median is nice but p95 under 400ms is the must-have for a good UX. p99 under 800ms would be great.
[00:04:35] Sofia: agree on p95 focus, but for long summarization TPOT matters — target cost and per-token speed, p95 token generation time under 8ms/token would be acceptable for us.
[00:04:48] Priya: when you say 8ms/token are you referencing single-GPU hosting? we should call out model variant — quantized 4-bit vs fp16 — those change the numbers a lot.
[00:04:58] Sofia: yeah we were thinking quantized to keep costs down.

[00:06:10] Alex: important to split the SLOs by route: interactive route SLO = TTFT p95 < 400ms, TTFT p99 < 800ms, and for heavy summarization route SLO = TPOT p95 < 8ms/token, TPOT p99 < 12ms/token. are those sensible starting points?
[00:06:27] Daniel: that sounds close. can we add a business SLA where overall error-rate and fallback rate to the old system are under 0.5%?
[00:06:36] Priya: yes we can track fallback rates and include them in acceptance criteria, we'll capture that as quality guardrail.

[00:08:00] Rajesh: question about measurement — do you recommend synthetic traffic or replaying production logs? we worry about PII in logs.
[00:08:09] Alex: replay is best for fidelity, but you can anonymize tokens or hash them. we also do hybrid: replay for sequence lengths and inter-arrival patterns, synthetic for stress runs.
[00:08:22] Sofia: we'll need a template from you for anonymization and also the schema for the replay harness.
[00:08:30] Alex: yes, we'll send the template. Priya, can you outline the recommended phases?
[00:08:36] Priya: phase 0: traffic export + analysis (measure token distributions, arrival rates, cold vs warm cache percent); phase 1: small-scale replay to validate runner and measurement hooks; phase 2: full 2-day sprint with ramp and burst tests, include both cold-start windows and warm cache baseline; phase 3: results analysis and tuning.
[00:09:00] Maria: from procurement perspective, how much runway does phase 2 need? like reserved capacity?
[00:09:06] Alex: for cost planning we can provide two options: hosted smoke-run (shorter but less isolated) or dedicated short-term reserved nodes for the sprint. we'll include both cost estimates in the template.

[00:10:22] Priya: measurement specifics: TTFT should be measured at the point of network ingress to the inference pool so we capture client-to-first-token. we also capture engine internal time-per-token (TPOT) from model emit hooks. for p95/p99 we recommend at least n=10k samples per route to have stable quantiles.
[00:10:45] Sofia: 10k samples per route — doable. how long to collect? with our traffic volume maybe 3 days for interactive, less for batch.
[00:10:55] Priya: right, and when measuring p99 you want to run over multiple windows to capture tail variability — we recommend a set of 1-hour windows across different load regimes.

[00:12:12] Alex: caching caveat — prefix/KV cache will dramatically improve TTFT for repeated prefixes. do you have a lot of repeated system prompts?
[00:12:20] Sofia: yes, about 35% of interactive starts share the same system prompt and user persona.
[00:12:27] Priya: then we'll record both cold-first-request and warm-cache percentiles. acceptance criteria should specify whether SLOs apply to warm or cold or both. most customers want warm p95 but also a cold-start p95 guardrail.
[00:12:40] Daniel: let's make interactive SLOs refer to warm cache p95 and cold p99, with an explicit note that warm p95 must be under 400ms.

[00:13:55] Rajesh: network noise question — will your measurement harness separate network latency vs model time? we need to know what to optimize (infra vs model config).
[00:14:04] Priya: we capture client-side timestamps and server-side engine timestamps. we'll send a mapping doc for the measurement hooks. network will be visible in ingress-to-engine delta; engine internal is the token generator time.
[00:14:14] Alex: we'll also instrument the KV cache hit/miss rate and batching stats; batching can change TPOT dramatically.

[00:15:40] Sofia: batching is tricky — interactive paths we want small batches or even single-request low latency pipeline; but long summaries can batch aggressively. can we measure batch size distribution during the recordings?
[00:15:50] Priya: yes, traffic analysis will include observed batching potential and recommend target batch sizes per route.

[00:17:05] Daniel: what about model variants and fallback — if the dedicated nodes are saturated do you have graceful fallback to smaller models?
[00:17:13] Alex: yes, Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback; for the pilot we can test a fallback policy: primary model -> quantized variant -> compact model. we'll measure degradation curves (latency vs quality).
[00:17:25] Sofia: measuring quality regressions is essential — we want automatic alerts if reranked outputs drop below thresholds.
[00:17:32] Priya: we'll pair latency runs with a small eval suite from your prompt set to track regressions. please include 50 golden prompts for regression checks.

[00:19:00] Alex: on sampling windows — recommend: baseline run for 1 hour at typical load, a ramp test to 2x for 30 minutes, and a burst test of 5 minutes at peak. combine multiple windows across a day.
[00:19:12] Rajesh: ok. and we'll need guidance on the runner infra — is it better to run the benchmark on our dedicated VPC or allow Redwood hosted runner?
[00:19:20] Priya: we support both. hosted runner is quickest; VPC runner gives fidelity for your network and compliance. for NovoMetric if you have data residency concerns, do the private runner.
[00:19:30] Maria: we do have a compliance checklist — SOC2 and ISO are required. do you have those docs?
[00:19:36] Alex: yes, we'll attach SOC2 attestation and our security whitepaper in the follow-up.

[00:20:50] Sofia: for p99 measurement stability, is there a recommended bootstrap? we worry p99 is noisy for small sample sizes.
[00:20:58] Priya: yep — use block bootstrapping across windows and require N>=10k samples per route; if you can't hit 10k, aggregate across similar windows and increase confidence intervals. we'll show stats scripts.

[00:22:10] Daniel: success criteria from product perspective — acceptable: interactive warm TTFT p95 < 400ms; unacceptable: user-facing fallbacks > 0.5% or p99 > 1s.
[00:22:22] Alex: capture that as pass/fail for the pilot. we'll also include cost per 1M tokens bucket so procurement has numbers.

[00:23:40] Priya: another measurement nuance: token accounting differences across models and tokenizers. include tokenization mapping in the export so we can normalize TPOT calculations.
[00:23:52] Sofia: good call — we'll include tokenizer id and model version for each sample.

[00:25:10] Rajesh: what about warm-up time for the model and KV cache; do we run a synthetic warm-up before measurement windows?
[00:25:19] Priya: yes, phase 2 will include a 10-minute warm-up period and we explicitly mark cold-window tests where we clear cache.

[00:26:40] Alex: timeline proposal — traffic export and analysis by Jul 18; infra prep by Jul 20; 2-day sprint week of Jul 24; results and tuning week of Jul 31. does that fit your go-live schedule?
[00:26:52] Daniel: we want a pilot decision by mid-August to plan budget. that timeline works.

[00:28:05] Maria: procurement needs high level statement of work, acceptance criteria, and pricing band. we can start internal approvals once we have those docs.
[00:28:15] Alex: we'll produce a short SOW and include the acceptance matrix (SLOs + quality + fallback thresholds).

[00:29:45] Priya: risk register quick notes: data sensitivity in replays (mitigate with hashing), bursty tails causing noisy p99s (mitigate with repeated windows), and network variability (mitigate with VPC runner).
[00:30:00] Sofia: any legal constraints on sending data outside the region? we'll check.

[00:31:20] Alex: measurement outputs we'll provide: per-route TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99, batching stats, KV cache hit rate, fallback rate, cost per 1M tokens, and a recommended production config (batching, quantization, routing).
[00:31:33] Daniel: can you provide a quick spreadsheet with estimated unit economics?
[00:31:38] Alex: yes, we'll include a unit-econ sheet template.

[00:33:05] Sofia: one subtle point — our annotators do occasional external API calls mid-conversation which add latency; should we strip those out of the baseline?
[00:33:15] Priya: mark those transactions as hybrid flows and measure separately; they shouldn't count against core model SLOs.

[00:34:40] Rajesh: for the VPC runner, do you support bringing your own key management? we need to ensure KMS integration for any token capture.
[00:34:48] Alex: yes, on private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations; we'll detail the key management options in the security packet.

[00:36:02] Maria: procurement question — if we do a dedicated reserved sprint, is there a minimal commitment?
[00:36:09] Alex: for short pilots we typically do a time-boxed reserved access with prorated billing, no long commit. production reservations have monthly minimums. we'll outline both.

[00:37:25] Priya: about analysis — when we report p99 we'll include the sample size and confidence interval and we will flag any windows where network jitter dominated.
[00:37:36] Sofia: ok makes sense.

[00:39:00] Daniel: what KPIs do you recommend we track post-pilot to validate rollout?
[00:39:07] Alex: 1) TTFT p95/p99 by route, 2) TPOT p95/p99 for heavy routes, 3) fallback rate, 4) cost per 1M tokens, 5) user response satisfaction (product metric).
[00:39:20] Sofia: we'll add token-efficiency (tokens per accepted answer) as a derived metric.

[00:40:50] Priya: ok last logistical asks: please share the replay schema, the anonymization guide, and the benchmark harness repo link.
[00:40:59] Alex: will do — expect a follow-up email by Jul 13 with docs and an initial SOW draft.

[00:41:30] Maria: once we get the SOW we'll route for budget sign-off.
[00:41:35] Daniel: anything else from the team?
[00:41:40] Sofia: can we include a small quality eval set (50 prompts) as priya suggested — we'll prepare that by Jul 18.
[00:41:47] Priya: perfect.

[00:43:00] Alex: recap of agreed SLOs for the pilot: interactive warm TTFT p95 < 400ms, interactive cold p99 < 800ms, summarization TPOT p95 < 8ms/token, TPOT p99 < 12ms/token; fallback rate < 0.5%. measurement: hybrid replay + synthetic, N>=10k samples per route, multiple windows.
[00:43:28] Daniel: marching orders sound good.

[00:45:05] Alex: we'll schedule the 2-day sprint, send invites — prefer Jul 24/25 currently.
[00:45:13] Rajesh: those dates work for infra.
[00:45:19] Maria: procurement will try to turn around the SOW approvals quickly.

[00:46:40] Priya: any competitor considerations we should watch in the benchmark? sometimes customers compare against LambdaServe perf numbers; we'll avoid public comparisons but we can run a neutral baseline.
[00:46:52] Sofia: only if it's apples-to-apples; tokenizers and model versions must match.

[00:48:10] Alex: ok final — I'll follow up with the template, SOW draft, and recommended runner options. Priya will own the bench harness prep.
[00:48:22] Priya: i'll send the harness link and a short README.
[00:48:28] Daniel: thanks all, looking forward.
[00:48:33] Maria: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
